title: Implement resilient cloud solutions
objective: Implement availability, scalability, and automated recovery based on failure scope, RTO/RPO, workload, and state.

sections.title: Mapping Availability Requirements to Failure Boundaries
paragraphs: A single-instance failure, an Availability Zone (AZ) failure, a Region failure, and accidental deletion each require different measures. The responsible team verifies the dependencies among compute, data, name resolution, authentication, and monitoring, and determines, together with the RTO/RPO, how much service must continue under each failure.

A multi-AZ deployment is meaningful only when failover for the data tier and entry points is designed as well. Simply adding redundant resources without defining health checks, switchover conditions, write consistency, and post-recovery verification does not guarantee automatic recovery.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: Resilient Cloud Solutions

sections.title: Scale using signals that indicate load
paragraphs: Scaling should not be determined solely by CPU utilization. Compare user demand, queue length, concurrency, latency, error rate, and processing time, and determine for each workload which signals indicate insufficient capacity.

Design the minimum, maximum, and desired capacity; the time required to scale out; warm-up; exclusion of unhealthy instances; and graceful-degradation behavior during sudden surges. An unlimited maximum does not guarantee availability; it hides the limits of dependencies and costs.

sections.title: Proving Recoverability Through Exercises
paragraphs: A backup success notification is not evidence that the RTO and RPO have been met. Execute the recovery responsibilities, restoration order, restore destination, data integrity checks, access permissions, traffic cutover, and failback, then compare the measured values with the targets.

Automated recovery is insufficient if it merely detects a failure and replaces resources. Verify that dependencies are available, configurations and secrets are passed correctly, the same failure is not repeated indefinitely, and metrics of user impact have improved.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: RTO/RPO and Automated Recovery

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for the ordering system wants it to continue operating during a single-AZ failure while minimizing data loss. Choose one most appropriate starting point for the design.

choices.text: Scale up the instance in a single AZ.
choices.explanation: This does not prepare for an AZ failure.

choices.text: Implement redundancy only, and decide the failover conditions after a failure occurs.
choices.explanation: The behavior of automatic recovery cannot be verified.

choices.text: Map the RTO/RPO, health checks, and failover for each of computing, data, entry points, and dependent services during an AZ failure.
choices.explanation: This allows continuity and consistency to be evaluated for each failure boundary.

checkpoints.prompt: Queue-processing wait times are increasing. Select the single most appropriate item that an operations professional should check when reviewing the scaling policy.

choices.text: Set the maximum capacity without limit based solely on CPU utilization.
choices.explanation: This ignores constraints on dependencies and costs.

choices.text: Do not record the queue length and keep the number of instances fixed at the same level every day.
choices.explanation: This cannot accommodate fluctuations in load.

choices.text: Review the queue length, processing time, request volume, latency, and error rate together with the minimum and maximum capacity and warm-up time over the same period.
choices.explanation: This makes it possible to link signals indicating insufficient capacity to scaling behavior.

checkpoints.prompt: A team validating a recovery plan wants to demonstrate that its backups are effective. Select the single most appropriate validation activity.

choices.text: Save only the success status shown for the backup job.
choices.explanation: This does not demonstrate recoverability or recovery time.

choices.text: Perform restoration, integrity checks, access-permission checks, traffic failover, and failback, then compare the measured RTO/RPO with the targets.
choices.explanation: This verifies whether operations can actually be resumed.

choices.text: Do not verify the configurations or secrets required during recovery.
choices.explanation: The service may not function after the replacement.
